hero.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
hero.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration from sending Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for isolation. The ruling prevents the US from using Kenya as a quarantine destination for its citizens who have had contact with the virus.

The United States has previously built specialized facilities within its own borders specifically for isolating people exposed to infectious diseases like Ebola. The country maintains the infrastructure and expertise to handle such cases domestically.

The court decision comes as the administration sought to use Kenya as an alternative location for quarantining exposed individuals. The proposed plan would have marked a departure from past practice, when the US constructed dedicated facilities on American soil to manage potential Ebola cases.

Ebola is a severe viral disease that spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected people. Outbreaks have primarily occurred in parts of Africa, though cases have occasionally appeared elsewhere through international travel. The virus causes fever, severe bleeding, and organ failure, with fatality rates that can exceed 50 percent in some outbreaks.

The US has dealt with Ebola cases before by building containment units at medical facilities. During the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak, American healthcare workers who contracted Ebola while working abroad were transported back to the US for treatment in specially designed isolation units.

The Kenyan court ruling effectively requires the US to handle quarantine and isolation of its own citizens exposed to the disease. Kenya has not publicly stated its reasons for opposing the arrangement through legal channels, but the court sided with objections to hosting potentially infected Americans.

This legal block creates logistical questions for how the US will manage future cases of Americans exposed to Ebola in regions where outbreaks occur. The administration has not announced alternative plans following the court decision.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran deal after White House meeting
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers but did not announce a final determination on a proposed Iran agreement after officials confirmed the two countries had agreed on a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers to make a final determination on an Iran proposal but did not announce a decision. US officials had previously confirmed that the United States and Iran agreed on a framework for a deal.

The White House stated that Trump will only support an agreement that satisfies his conditions. The administration called the meeting to evaluate the Iran proposal.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as U.S. and Iran Edge Closer to Agreement
cards.body:
Oil prices dropped below $100 a barrel as investors responded to reports that the United States and Iran are moving closer to a potential peace agreement. Brent crude futures, which serve as the global oil benchmark, fell 6 percent to $97.43 per barrel, marking the lowest level in two weeks. The decline reflected market optimism that a deal to end the conflict could be reached.

Stock markets rose on the news. Japan's Nikkei index climbed nearly 3 percent, while the pan-European Stoxx 600 index gained 1 percent. Several major markets, including the United States and United Kingdom, were closed for a public holiday on Monday.

Despite progress in negotiations, significant obstacles remain. While a framework has been negotiated between Washington and Tehran, the two sides continue to disagree on critical issues. Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remains a major sticking point. An Iranian government spokesperson cautioned that an agreement was "not imminent," signaling that a deal is far from certain.

Warren Patterson, head of commodities strategy at ING, warned against overreacting to the diplomatic signals. "We've been at this stage before, only for talks to break down. Therefore, the market will likely be more cautious about overreacting," he told Reuters.

Even if negotiations succeed and the strait reopens, analysts expect the recovery to take considerable time. Damaged energy infrastructure in Qatar and other regions will require months to repair. Physical oil flows through the strategic waterway remain restricted, according to UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, who emphasized that actual changes to oil supply are what matter most for markets.

Shipping data showed limited signs of resumed activity. Two tankers carrying liquefied natural gas departed the strait on Monday heading to Pakistan and China, while an Iraqi crude supertanker that had been stranded for nearly three months left the Gulf for China on Saturday.

Current oil prices remain substantially higher than before the conflict began in late February, when Brent crude traded around $70 per barrel. The elevated prices have contributed to broader inflation concerns worldwide. Rising costs for oil, gas, fertilizer, and other materials are expected to drive food prices higher in coming months.

These inflation worries have shifted market expectations regarding interest rates. Before the Iran conflict, traders anticipated central bank rate cuts. Now they predict rate increases instead. Markets currently expect the Bank of England to raise rates twice this year.

Other markets responded positively to the ceasefire prospects. Gold climbed 1.46 percent to $4,574 per ounce, while the pound gained almost 0.6 percent against the dollar, reaching $1.3506. Stephen Innes, an independent analyst, noted that the market reaction reflected investors pricing in the possibility that a critical global energy chokepoint could soon return to normal operations.

cards.headline: Ukraine prepares for major Russian attacks in coming hours
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is bracing for large-scale Russian strikes within the next 24 hours.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Ukraine is bracing for major Russian attacks within the next 24 hours as tensions escalate along the front lines.

The warning coincides with increased Russian military activity. A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people. Russian officials have cautioned Europe to prepare for additional drone incidents in the region.

cards.headline: UN adds Israel and Russia to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: Israeli and Russian forces were placed on the United Nations list for sexual violence in conflict zones.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israel and Russia to its blacklist for sexual violence in armed conflict. The decision followed a UN report documenting abuse by security forces, including the rape of male detainees.

UN investigators verified sexual abuse of 31 Palestinian men, women and children from Gaza and the occupied West Bank between 2023 and 2025. The report documented repeated gang-rapes and the use of sexual violence as torture by Israeli forces. Israel announced it would cut ties with the UN chief over its inclusion on the blacklist, which identifies parties credibly suspected of committing sexual violence in conflict situations.

cards.headline: Iran hard-liners stage rallies to oppose potential US deal
cards.teaser: A faction within Iran has used rallies, state media, and statements in an attempt to undermine negotiations with the United States.
cards.body:
A vocal faction of hard-liners in Iran is working to block negotiations with the United States. They have organized rallies and leveraged state media to oppose the talks, issuing both public and private statements against the negotiation process.

US and Iranian officials have agreed on a framework for a potential deal. President Trump met with his advisers to make a final determination on the agreement, though no deal has been formally announced yet.

cards.headline: EU unlocks 16.4 billion euros for Hungary under new prime minister
cards.teaser: The European Commission released funds previously frozen under the prior government, hailing what it called a wind of change in Hungary.
cards.body:
The European Union has agreed to release 16.4 billion euros to Hungary that were frozen under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the decision alongside Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who took office less than three weeks ago. The funds had been withheld due to rule of law and corruption concerns.

The breakthrough coincides with other positive developments in Hungary's governance. Police have announced they will permit Budapest's Pride parade to proceed next month, reversing the previous government's policy of blocking the event. Magyar has described the EU decision as a historic breakthrough, reflecting the EU's view that the new administration represents a meaningful shift in the country's direction.

hero.headline: Russian drone strikes apartment building in Romania, injuring civilians
hero.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in Galați, Romania on Friday during overnight attacks on Ukraine, injuring two people in what officials described as a serious escalation of the conflict's spillover effects into NATO territory.

The drone struck the roof of the residential building, sparking a fire and forcing the evacuation of several residents. Romanian authorities confirmed the strike represented the first time civilians have been injured by such an incursion into Romanian territory since the war began.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded swiftly, stating the alliance is "ready to defend every inch" of allied territory. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte wrote on social media after speaking with Romanian President Nicuşor Dan.

Romanian officials responded with serious consequences. Dan convened an emergency meeting of the country's supreme council of national defence and instructed the foreign ministry to prepare measures regarding Romania's relationship with Moscow that would be "proportionate to this very serious situation." The foreign ministry summoned Russia's ambassador and described the incident as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and serious breach of international law.

Romania's foreign minister, Oana Țoiu, warned of diplomatic repercussions. "We will officially communicate the consequences that this lack of responsibility on the part of the Russian Federation will have for the diplomatic relations between our countries, as well as the next steps at the European level regarding sanctions packages," she said.

Romania has asked NATO to accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities and indicated it would invoke Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions about threats to member security.

General Gheorghe Maxim, a Romanian armed forces commander, clarified the strike was not a direct military attack but emphasized that "Romanians should understand that Russia is a threat to the security of the countries in the area."

Putin claimed he had only just learned of the incident and suggested without evidence that the drone might have been a stray Ukrainian weapon. He requested that drone wreckage be handed to Russia for independent investigation.

The incident drew condemnation from European and international leaders. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line" and pledged full solidarity with Romania. France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot denounced the "irresponsible act by Russia."

The Romanian military scrambled two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter authorized to engage targets in response. Galați, located on the Danube River west of the borders with Moldova and Ukraine, has increasingly faced drone incursions as Russian forces intensify strikes in southern Ukraine near the Romanian border.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran proposal after White House meeting
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers for two hours about a possible arrangement after officials confirmed the US and Iran had agreed on a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump spent two hours meeting with advisers at the White House to discuss a potential Iran agreement. The discussion centered on a possible extension of a ceasefire arrangement after US and Iran officials had reached a framework for a deal.

Trump had signaled on social media that he was prepared to announce a final decision following the meeting. However, no announcement was made after the discussions concluded.

cards.headline: Ukrainian officials say nine-year-old components found in Russian Oreshnik missile
cards.teaser: Ukraine examined parts from a Russian Oreshnik missile fired in January and determined some components were manufactured nine years ago.
cards.body:
Ukrainian experts who examined debris from a Russian Oreshnik missile launched in January discovered components manufactured nearly a decade ago. The discovery contradicts Russian claims about the weapon's technological sophistication.

Ukrainian officials also reported that roughly a quarter of American components found in Russian weapons are counterfeit. The missile contained Belarusian-made parts and was equipped with kinetic penetrators as its warhead.

cards.headline: First person rescued from flooded Laos cave after nine days
cards.teaser: A man was led to safety by rescuers after being stranded in a flooded cavern for nine days, the first of five trapped individuals.
cards.body:
Rescuers have successfully extracted the first of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week underground. The rescue operation involved divers navigating through narrow, water-filled tunnels filled with sharp rocks and collapse hazards.

Four of the men remain inside a chamber about 300 metres from the cave entrance, where they were found huddled together on a rocky ledge. Two others are still missing. An international team of rescue divers, including some who participated in the 2018 Thai football team cave rescue, has been deployed to extract the remaining survivors.

cards.headline: Iran hard-liners stage rallies to oppose potential US deal
cards.teaser: A faction within Iran has used rallies, state media, and statements in an attempt to undermine negotiations with the United States.
cards.body:
A vocal faction of hard-liners in Iran is working to block negotiations with the United States. They have organized rallies and leveraged state media to oppose the talks, issuing both public and private statements against the negotiation process.

US and Iranian officials have agreed on a framework for a potential deal. President Trump met with his advisers to make a final determination on the agreement, though no deal has been formally announced yet.

hero.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration plan to add president's name to Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered the removal of Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, ruling that the Washington DC venue cannot be renamed without an act of Congress.

US District Judge Christopher Cooper issued a 94-page ruling on Friday stating that it was "crystal clear" the performing arts complex was named for the late President John F. Kennedy. The judge directed the Trump administration to remove all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days.

The decision also blocked the Trump administration's plan to close the Kennedy Center for two years of extensive renovations. The judge found that the Kennedy Center board violated legal requirements when it voted to approve both the renaming and the operational shutdown.

The Kennedy Center was established by Congress and operates under specific statutory requirements that govern how it functions as the nation's cultural center in Washington. The facility hosts theater, dance, orchestral performances and other arts programming. The court determined that changes to the building's name and operational status violated these legal requirements.

Following the court defeat, Trump responded by saying he has "no interest" in the Kennedy Center. The president's initial plans had included substantial changes to the venue, with the two-year renovation period set to shut down performances and events during that time.

The ruling addresses two separate issues that the Kennedy Center board had approved: the renaming of the building and the planned closure for renovations. The judge found legal problems with both decisions.

Trump announced his intention to withdraw from involvement with the Kennedy Center after the judicial decision. The administration has not indicated whether it will appeal the ruling or pursue alternative plans for the facility.

The Kennedy Center serves as the national performing arts venue in Washington, hosting major cultural events and programming throughout the year. Congress created the institution and established the legal framework under which it operates, which the judge cited in blocking the administration's proposed changes.

The decision means the Kennedy Center must continue operating under its established name and maintain its current programming schedule. The two-year closure plan cannot proceed under the court's current ruling.

This case represents a significant legal setback for the Trump administration's effort to reshape the iconic arts institution. The judge's interpretation of the legal requirements governing the Kennedy Center establishes that Congressional action would be necessary for any future name changes to the building.

cards.headline: Judge temporarily blocks Justice Department fund for alleged weaponization victims
cards.teaser: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration from immediately implementing a $1.8 billion fund intended to compensate people who claim they were targeted by government agencies.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Virginia temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring money into an $1.8 billion fund designed to compensate alleged victims of government weaponization. U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema issued the order on Friday, barring the government from taking further action in creating or operating the fund while legal challenges proceed.

The order prevents funds from being irreversibly distributed from what the administration calls the Anti-Weaponization fund. The temporary block remains in effect while the court hears arguments in the case challenging the fund's establishment.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran deal after White House meeting
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers but did not announce a final determination on a proposed Iran agreement after officials confirmed the two countries had agreed on a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers to make a final determination on an Iran proposal but did not announce a decision. US officials had previously confirmed that the United States and Iran agreed on a framework for a deal.

The White House stated that Trump will only support an agreement that satisfies his conditions. The administration called the meeting to evaluate the Iran proposal.

cards.headline: ICE agent charged in Minneapolis shooting arrested in Texas
cards.teaser: A US immigration agent wanted for a shooting during an immigration enforcement operation in Minneapolis was captured in Texas.
cards.body:
An ICE agent named Christian Castro was arrested in Texas on Friday, 11 days after being charged by Minneapolis prosecutors. Castro faces charges of assault and falsely reporting a crime in connection with a shooting in Minnesota.

The incident involved a Venezuelan man and occurred during a sweeping immigration enforcement operation in the Minneapolis area. Video evidence of the non-fatal shooting emerged, leading to the charges against Castro.

cards.headline: Airlines warn against restricting international flights over sanctuary city dispute
cards.teaser: Airlines and business groups cautioned that limits on international flights would create chaos as DHS considers punishing sanctuary jurisdictions through airport actions.
cards.body:
Airlines and business groups have warned that restricting international flights would create widespread disruption, opposing a plan by DHS Secretary Mullin to punish sanctuary jurisdictions by targeting their airports. Mullin previously threatened to pull agents from Newark airport following protests at an ICE detention center.

The travel industry has urged the Trump administration to abandon any curbs on international flights as part of the escalating dispute over sanctuary cities.

cards.headline: Violence and protests escalate at New Jersey immigration detention facility
cards.teaser: Reports of broken fingers and targeted attacks on journalists emerged from protests outside the Delaney Hall ICE detention center in Newark.
cards.body:
Photojournalists said ICE agents targeted them during clashes outside the Delaney Hall detention facility in Newark. Reporters described broken fingers and damaged cameras during the confrontation.

New Jersey officials announced that state police will take over policing operations from federal immigration officers at Delaney Hall. Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport said state police will establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators as part of efforts to lower tensions at the site, where protests and a hunger strike have been ongoing.

cards.headline: Three climbers dead after fall on Alaska's Mount McKinley
cards.teaser: Three climbers who fell near a treacherous pass on Mount McKinley died, while one person was rescued from the mountain.
cards.body:
Three climbers died after falling near a treacherous pass on Mount McKinley, also known as Denali, North America's highest peak. One member of the climbing party was rescued from the incident.

The accident occurred at one of the mountain's most dangerous passages, which poses significant risks to climbers navigating the route.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes on Florida Launchpad During Test
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin rocket exploded on a Florida launchpad during testing, affecting stock prices of space industry companies.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a "hotfire" test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad at Kennedy Space Center, with the orange sky visible over 115 miles away in Fort Pierce. Blue Origin confirmed that no personnel were harmed and described the incident as an "anomaly."

The explosion poses challenges for NASA's lunar program, which depends on Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket for planned missions to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon within the next two years.

cards.headline: Universal Music Group Rejects Bill Ackman's Takeover Bid
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a takeover proposal from billionaire Bill Ackman's Pershing Square investment firm.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group has rejected a takeover proposal from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management, valued at approximately $64-65 billion. The company's board determined the offer fundamentally and materially undervalued the business and declined to proceed with the terms presented.

Universal Music Group remains one of the world's largest music companies, controlling a significant portion of the global recorded music market.

cards.headline: Dell Stock Soars on AI Server Sales Outlook
cards.teaser: Dell shares rose nearly 40 percent after the company reported strong results driven by artificial intelligence server demand.
cards.body:
Dell stock jumped nearly 40 percent following a quarterly report that exceeded expectations. The company's performance was fueled by strong demand for servers used in artificial intelligence applications.

The rally marked Dell's best single-day gain in two years. Michael Dell's personal fortune increased by $34 billion as a result of the stock surge, making him richer than Mark Zuckerberg. The results boosted shares of other server makers and helped push technology indexes to record highs.

cards.headline: Stock Indexes Close at Record Highs on Technology Gains
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 rose for a ninth consecutive week as technology stocks led markets to new closing records.
cards.body:
Major stock indexes hit new closing highs as technology companies gained. The S&P 500 rose for a ninth straight week, the longest winning streak since 2023. Dell led advances in the Nasdaq, which reached record levels.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average also closed higher amid optimism about a potential Middle East agreement. Wall Street extended its rally on the strength of technology sector performance and investor sentiment about diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran.

cards.headline: UnitedHealthcare Removes Prior Approval for Most Pediatric Services
cards.teaser: UnitedHealthcare will eliminate insurance approval requirements for nearly two-thirds of pediatric medical services.
cards.body:
UnitedHealthcare announced it will remove prior authorization requirements for most pediatric services. The insurer will eliminate approval steps for nearly two-thirds of children's medical care.

The policy change affects a significant portion of pediatric healthcare services covered by UnitedHealthcare plans. The company made the decision to reduce administrative requirements for doctors treating children covered under its insurance policies.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Allows Tax Avoidance Through Foreign Havens
cards.teaser: U.S. companies avoided at least $40 billion in taxes since early 2025 using schemes in countries including Malta and Cyprus.
cards.body:
The Trump administration cleared the way for U.S. companies to avoid taxes through foreign havens. American corporations skirted at least $40 billion in tax payments since the beginning of 2025.

Companies used tax schemes in Malta, Bermuda, Cyprus, and other jurisdictions to reduce their U.S. tax obligations. The arrangements allowed businesses to shift profits to lower-tax countries, reducing their overall tax burden on earnings.

cards.headline: SpaceX awarded $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The company disclosed that government contracts accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue in its IPO filing.
cards.body:
SpaceX received $6.45 billion in contracts from the US Space Force, according to disclosures made in the company's IPO filing. The awards represent a major component of SpaceX's government business operations.

The filing revealed that government contracts accounted for one-fifth of SpaceX's total revenue in 2025. The company is proceeding with its plans to go public after operating as a private enterprise for years.

cards.headline: Law enforcement dismantles botnet controlling over 17 million devices
cards.teaser: The botnet was linked to a residential proxy network based in Russia.
cards.body:
Authorities have taken down a botnet that had infected more than 17 million devices worldwide. The operation targeted what investigators described as one of the largest known botnets in recent years.

The botnet was reportedly connected to a Russia-based residential proxy network. Such networks route internet traffic through infected home devices, allowing operators to mask their online activities and locations by using the IP addresses of unwitting victims.

cards.headline: Texas measles outbreak analysis shows one in five cases hospitalized
cards.teaser: Most hospitalized patients developed complications from the virus.
cards.body:
A measles outbreak in Texas revealed that approximately one in five cases required hospitalization. The majority of hospitalized patients experienced complications from their infections.

Measles poses serious health threats, potentially causing pneumonia, brain inflammation, and rarely death. Young children and immunocompromised individuals face particular risk from the highly contagious virus.

cards.headline: Coders increasingly refuse to work without AI assistance
cards.teaser: Researchers warn that AI may help programmers write code faster but not necessarily better.
cards.body:
Software developers are increasingly unwilling to work on projects that don't permit AI coding assistants. This shift reflects the rapid integration of these tools into programming workflows over the past year or two.

However, researchers caution that speed gains don't necessarily translate to quality improvements. While AI assistants help programmers write code faster, the output may not be better constructed. This focus on velocity over careful development could create technical problems in the future as more software relies on AI-assisted creation.

cards.headline: FCC warns broadcasters to follow orders or face punishment like ABC
cards.teaser: ABC said the early renewal imposed on all its stations is unprecedented and serves no legitimate purpose.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission under the Trump administration has warned all broadcasters to comply with its directives or face consequences similar to those imposed on ABC. The warning signals a more aggressive regulatory stance toward television networks.

ABC stated that the FCC's decision to require early license renewal for all of its stations is unprecedented in broadcast regulation. The network said the action has no legitimate regulatory purpose and appears punitive in nature.

cards.headline: Justice Department sues states over rejected ICE undercover license plate requests
cards.teaser: The DOJ has accused ICE monitoring sites of doxing agents, but has provided little evidence to support the claim.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has filed lawsuits against states that refused to issue undercover license plates for Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The legal action seeks to compel state compliance with federal immigration enforcement requests.

The DOJ has repeatedly accused websites that monitor ICE activities of doxing agents by publishing their personal information. The department has offered limited evidence to support these allegations.

hero.headline: Joao Fonseca upsets Novak Djokovic at French Open
hero.body:
Brazilian teenager Joao Fonseca defeated Novak Djokovic in five sets at the French Open, eliminating the Serbian champion in the third round. The 19-year-old rallied to beat Djokovic, ending the veteran's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title.

The match marked a significant upset at Roland Garros, where Djokovic entered as one of the favorites. Fonseca's victory represents a breakthrough moment for the young player, who defeated one of tennis's most decorated champions on one of the sport's biggest stages.

Djokovic, who has won 24 Grand Slam singles titles, has been competing at the highest level for nearly two decades. The loss comes as he pursues what would be a record-extending 25th major championship.

The French Open has seen multiple favorites fall in the early rounds this year. Fonseca's win over Djokovic continues that trend and represents one of the tournament's most notable results.

Fonseca turned professional recently and has been rising through the tennis rankings. The win over Djokovic provides validation of his talent and potential at the sport's top level.

The five-set format of Grand Slam matches tests both physical endurance and mental resilience. Fonseca demonstrated both qualities in coming back to defeat Djokovic after losing early in the match.

Djokovic's tournament exit opens the draw for other players seeking the French Open title. The Serbian had been attempting to add to his collection of major championships and extend his place in tennis history.

For Fonseca, the victory represents the biggest win of his young career. Defeating a player of Djokovic's caliber on clay at Roland Garros establishes the Brazilian as a serious competitor in professional tennis.

cards.headline: Steelers fire assistant coach Derius Swinton II for workplace misconduct
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh Steelers dismissed assistant special teams coach Derius Swinton II for violating club policy.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers fired assistant special teams coach Derius Swinton II for workplace misconduct, ending his tenure after just over three months on the job. The team cited a violation of club policy in parting ways with Swinton.

Swinton was hired earlier this year as part of the Steelers' coaching staff. His dismissal comes less than a year after he joined the organization.

cards.headline: MLB suspends Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe for gesture toward Cardinals
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball suspended Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe for one game over actions during a game against the St. Louis Cardinals.
cards.body:
MLB handed Abner Uribe a one-game suspension for what the league called an inappropriate gesture toward the Cardinals during a Brewers victory. Uribe made a celebration gesture on video that led to the disciplinary action.

The Brewers pitcher is appealing the suspension. The incident occurred during Milwaukee's win over St. Louis, when Uribe performed what has been described as a DX chop celebration.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and Abdul Carter address Trump disagreement
cards.teaser: New York Giants players Jaxson Dart and Abdul Carter expressed unity after a public disagreement over former President Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and defensive player Abdul Carter discussed their viewpoints following a disagreement about Trump. Carter called out Dart to demonstrate his opposition to the former president, while Dart had introduced Trump at an event.

Dart addressed the team during a meeting to discuss his introduction of Trump. The two players worked to express unity despite their different political positions on the matter.

cards.headline: Sacramento launches bid for MLB expansion team
cards.teaser: A Sacramento group has begun efforts to bring a Major League Baseball expansion team to the California city.
cards.body:
Sacramento investors have launched a formal bid to bring Major League Baseball to the region as part of MLB's expansion efforts. The investor group is working to position Sacramento as a viable market for a new franchise.

The city is competing against other locations, including Vancouver, for expansion consideration. Local fans have demonstrated enthusiasm for a major league presence in the area, signaling community support for the initiative.

cards.headline: NCAA baseball tournament regionals underway
cards.teaser: The 2026 NCAA baseball tournament has reached the regional rounds, with teams competing for spots in the College World Series.
cards.body:
Regional games in the NCAA baseball tournament began, with 64 teams competing across 16 regional sites. The winners will advance to super regionals as the field narrows toward the College World Series in Omaha.

The tournament bracket features top-seeded teams hosting regional competitions. Players and teams are competing in the single-elimination format that characterizes the NCAA postseason.

cards.headline: Glasgow Warriors advance to URC semi-finals with win over Connacht
cards.teaser: Glasgow Warriors defeated Connacht to secure a spot in the United Rugby Championship semi-finals.
cards.body:
Glasgow Warriors advanced to the URC semi-finals after securing a hard-fought victory over Connacht. The win sets up a semi-final clash against either Bulls or Munster, depending on the outcome of their quarter-final match.

The Warriors' triumph keeps their championship ambitions on track as the United Rugby Championship enters its decisive stages.

hero.headline: Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor Marcia Lucas Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the film editor who won an Academy Award for editing Star Wars and helped shape several influential films of the 1970s, died on Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer. Lucas was the former wife of Star Wars director George Lucas.

Lucas won her Oscar for editing the original Star Wars film. Her work on the landmark 1977 science fiction movie contributed to its success as one of the most influential films in cinema history.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited several other notable films during the 1970s, a period when she established herself as a significant figure in Hollywood post-production. Her editing work helped define the visual storytelling of an era that transformed American cinema.

Lucas worked during a time when few women held prominent technical roles in film production. Her success as an editor broke barriers in an industry dominated by men, and her Oscar win recognized both her technical skill and creative vision.

The family described her as a brilliant storyteller and a trailblazer in her field. Her contributions to Star Wars extended beyond technical editing to include shaping the narrative structure that made the film resonate with audiences worldwide.

Lucas was married to George Lucas during the production of Star Wars and several other films from that period. The couple later divorced.

Her death removes one of the last surviving key creative figures from the original Star Wars production team. The film's success launched a franchise that has continued for nearly five decades and fundamentally changed how Hollywood approaches blockbuster filmmaking.

Lucas spent her later years in Rancho Mirage, a desert community in Southern California known as a retirement destination for entertainment industry figures.

cards.headline: More Than Half of Performers Drop Out of Great American State Fair Concert
cards.teaser: Artists have withdrawn from a planned Trump-linked Freedom 250 concert amid political controversy and reported threats.
cards.body:
More than half of the nine featured performers scheduled for the Freedom 250 concert series have withdrawn from the events. The concerts are part of Trump administration-organized celebrations marking the United States' 250th anniversary.

At least seven musical acts have dropped out within 48 hours of the lineup announcement. Bret Michaels was among the latest to withdraw, citing a deteriorating atmosphere around the event and threats being made. Other performers who canceled include Morris Day and Young MC.

cards.headline: A24 Horror Film Backrooms Earns Over $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The debut feature from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons opened in theaters nationwide after strong preview screenings.
cards.body:
Backrooms, a horror film from A24 and first-time director Kane Parsons, grossed more than $10 million in preview screenings. The movie opened in theaters nationwide and is expected to perform well at the box office.

Parsons, who is 20 years old, directed the film based on a YouTube series concept. The cast includes Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Mark Duplass, Finn Bennett, Avan Jogia, and Lukita Maxwell.

cards.headline: Trump Criticizes Judge Over Kennedy Center Ruling, Plans Congressional Transfer
cards.teaser: The president responded to a court order that halted renovations and removed his name from the performing arts institution.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump criticized a judge's ruling that ordered his name removed from the Kennedy Center and blocked planned renovations. The judge's 94-page decision stated it was "crystal clear" that the performing arts venue was named after President John F. Kennedy.

The ruling also prevented the Kennedy Center from closing for the two-year renovation period Trump had announced. Following the decision, Trump said he plans to transfer control of the institution to Congress.

cards.headline: L.A. Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman called for uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production in the final days before Tuesday's election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman urged candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production. Raman made the appeal on Friday, days before the Tuesday election.

Raman appeared outside Radford Studios with entertainment figures who support her mayoral campaign, including Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon. She advocated for policies to ensure Hollywood remains a production hub.

cards.headline: Judge Reinstates Defamation Judgment Against Blogger in Megan Thee Stallion Case
cards.teaser: A court found blogger Milagro Gramz was commissioned by Tory Lanez's family and lost media protections for certain statements.
cards.body:
A judge has reinstated a defamation judgment against blogger Milagro Gramz in a case involving rapper Megan Thee Stallion. The court determined that Gramz was commissioned by Tory Lanez's family to make statements branding Megan a liar.

Because of this relationship, the judge ruled that Gramz did not qualify for media defendant protections for those statements. The ruling restores a previous judgment in Megan Thee Stallion's favor.

cards.headline: Kanye West Cleared to Perform in Netherlands on His Birthday
cards.teaser: Dutch officials ruled insufficient evidence existed to ban the rapper from entering the country.
cards.body:
Officials in the Netherlands cleared Kanye West to perform in the country on his birthday. Authorities ruled that insufficient evidence had been found to ban the rapper from entering.

The decision allows West to proceed with a scheduled performance.

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington D.C. ordered President Trump to remove his name from the Kennedy Center within two weeks, ruling that the performing arts venue cannot be renamed without an act of Congress.

U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper signed the order Friday, concluding that the Kennedy Center board exceeded its legal authority by unilaterally renaming the facility after Trump. In his 94-page ruling, Cooper wrote that it was "crystal clear" that Congress deliberately designated the arts complex as the "John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts" in 1964.

"The Court has concluded that the Board overstepped its statutory bounds by unilaterally renaming the Kennedy Center after President Trump," Cooper wrote in the decision.

Under the court order, Trump has 14 days to remove his name from all physical signage at the building and to eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials.

The ruling also blocks the performing arts venue from implementing a planned two-year closure for extensive renovations. The closure had been scheduled to begin later this year. By halting this closure, at least temporarily, the Kennedy Center will continue its current programming while the legal dispute continues.

The decision represents a significant setback to the administration's effort to renovate the performing arts venue. The Kennedy Center board had previously approved adding Trump's name to the facility as part of these renovation plans.

Members of the Kennedy family celebrated the ruling, which came on Friday, the birthday of President John F. Kennedy. "An appropriate birthday present on my uncle's birthday today," wrote Maria Shriver, JFK's niece. "A federal judge ruled that President Trump and the Kennedy Center Board acted unlawfully in renaming the Kennedy Center. The judge held that only Congress can change the Center's name and blocked the planned two-year closure."

Kerry Kennedy, Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s daughter, wrote on social media: "Perhaps I won't need that pickaxe after all. What a great way to celebrate you on your birthday, Uncle Jack!"

Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's health secretary, made no immediate public comment on the ruling.

Joe Kennedy III, a former congressman and grandson of Robert F. Kennedy, had previously called the name change illegal. "The Kennedy Center is a living memorial to a fallen president and named for President Kennedy by federal law," he wrote in December when the renaming was first announced. "It can no sooner be renamed than can someone rename the Lincoln Memorial, no matter what anyone says."

The judge's decision examined the statutory framework governing the Kennedy Center and determined that the board lacked the authority to change the facility's name without additional congressional authorization.

cards.headline: Federal judge reopens Trump IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS after intervenors challenged a settlement agreement.
cards.body: A federal judge in Florida ruled to reopen President Trump's lawsuit seeking $10 billion from the IRS. The judge sided with intervenors who challenged a settlement agreement between the Department of Justice and Trump that would have dismissed the case in exchange for creating an "anti-weaponization" fund. The judge determined that this settlement arrangement had compromised the integrity of the case and warranted further review.

cards.headline: Pentagon awards $9.7 billion Dell contract amid conflict concerns
cards.teaser: The Defense Department's new contract with Dell raised questions after President Trump promoted the company's products and purchased its stock.
cards.body:
The Pentagon announced a five-year, $9.7 billion contract with Dell for Microsoft software and cloud services as part of an effort to consolidate technology services across the Department of Defense.

The agreement raised questions about potential conflicts of interest. President Trump had previously promoted Dell's products publicly and purchased significant amounts of the company's stock before the contract was awarded.

cards.headline: New Jersey detention facility becomes test for DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: Protests and a reported hunger strike at Delaney Hall mark the first major immigration clash under the new Homeland Security secretary.
cards.body:
A private detention center in Newark, New Jersey has become a flashpoint in disputes over Trump administration immigration policies, representing the first major test for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's leadership.

Protesters have been arrested outside the 1,000-bed Delaney Hall Facility while detainees reportedly participate in a hunger strike over claims of inhumane living conditions and inadequate medical care. In response to escalating tensions, New Jersey's governor announced that state police will take over policing functions from federal immigration officers at the site. The state plans to establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators as part of efforts to lower the temperature at the facility.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary backs putting Trump on $250 bill
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent endorsed a proposed $250 bill featuring President Trump to commemorate the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait, saying it would celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The White House is pushing Congress to approve the commemorative currency, and the Treasury Department has already begun preparations for the possibility.

The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on US currency. Democrats have vowed to block the move, while Bessent made his endorsement during a Friday appearance where Fox Business contributor Larry Kudlow posed the question about the proposed bill.

cards.headline: Bulgaria to end US military aircraft stay over visa dispute
cards.teaser: Bulgaria will cut the stay of U.S. military aircraft at the end of June after the Trump administration did not approve visa-free travel for Bulgarians.
cards.body:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced Friday that his country will end the presence of U.S. military aircraft in Sofia by the end of June. The decision follows the Trump administration's refusal to grant Bulgarian citizens visa-free travel to the United States.

Radev had previously called for the suspension of visas for Bulgarian citizens during discussions with U.S. officials. The move reflects escalating tensions between the two countries over their visa program disagreement.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by 3 points in Texas race poll
cards.teaser: Democrat James Talarico holds a narrow lead over Republican Ken Paxton in a new poll of likely Texas voters.
cards.body:
State Representative James Talarico holds a slight edge in the Texas Senate race, according to a poll released by Texas Public Opinion Research. Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico compared to 44 percent for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

The poll shows the Democratic candidate leading his Republican opponent by three percentage points. The survey was conducted following the runoff election in the state.
